content.transcript: Urban trees can make cities more comfortable during hot weather. Their leaves provide shade, while evaporation from vegetation can reduce local temperatures. However, planting trees is not enough by itself. Young trees need water and maintenance, and planners must choose species that suit the local climate. The lecture therefore argues that successful urban greening requires both planting and long-term care.

key_points: species should suit the local climate
